chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Family shows for doctors and nurses
summary: Green explains that performing for staff families was like passing the staff, with a show made up of patients.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I don't understand exactly what you mean when you say it's the height of someone's personality.
Well, personality is the appearance of a human being's physical whereabouts, going and coming. (Laughter)
Yes. So?
You have to have something to pray with, (Laughter) you understand? If you get up off your knees, you done said your prayers.
Well, why those family shows -- the height of someone's personality?
Well, that's because -- that's our seniorities, you see. The family is the tree of life, you know, Family resemblance, you know.
So, what you're saying basically is that a family show is a representation of a family?
No, that families would arrive -- they were the audience. Families -- doctors' families, nurses' families, and so on like that.

It gave you more feeling of well-being because of their profession, like, because they were doctors and nurses being so helpful to people -- did this make you want to make them feel happy, or do what you could -- or are we way off?
Well, no, --
I think what he's saying --
No, no. See, doctors are curers, you know,
they're healers, and so are nurses.
Yes.
If they're fortunate.
Yes, yes.
Well, now, say for instance that if you're a patient in their care, you see, and you have earned the privilege of performing, see, where they would -- for their observation --
Yes, yes.
You see, that's like passing the staff.
So, you were performing for those people.
Yes, was quite a lot of us. We had our own show there, you know. But the show was made up of patients.
